identity.name: Hamdanid dynasty (emirates of Mosul and Aleppo)

land.text: Mosul and Diyar Bakr, the governorship of Hasan Nasir al-Dawla

predecessors.note: The Hamdanids were the caliph's governors: the Abbasid dossier records them as vassals from 929 to 947. The infobox 'Preceded by' is the Abbasid Caliphate.

successors.note: 990 (the page: 'divided between the Uqaylids and the Marwanids').

land.text: the Marwanid share of the former Hamdanid area
Aleppo and northern Syria, under Lu'lu' who 'acknowledged [al-Aziz] as Caliph' in 995

successors.note: Infobox 'Succeeded by: Uqaylid dynasty, Fatimid Caliphate, Mirdasid dynasty'; the Emirate of Aleppo page has Aleppo 'falling to the Fatimids in 1017'.
Listed as a successor in the infobox; none of the pages opened dates the Mirdasid take-over.

capitals.name: Mosul
capitals.note: Infobox 'Mosul (905–990)'; Nasir al-Dawla's seat for the Jazira.

capitals.name: Aleppo
capitals.note: Infobox 'Aleppo (944–1002)'; extended to the 1004 end. Sayf al-Dawla's second seat was Mayyafariqin (Sayf al-Dawla page).

correction.text: Mosul and Diyar Bakr, the governorship of Hasan Nasir al-Dawla ('governor of Mosul and Diyar Bakr')

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria's first Hamdanid shape begins in 936 but the page dates Nasir al-Dawla's rule at Mosul and Diyar Bakr from 929 ('The rule of Hassan Nasir al-Dawla (929–968), governor of Mosul and Diyar Bakr'). The Nasir al-Dawla page has his troops occupy Mosul in 934 and the caliph recognise him in late 935, so the 929-933 span is the page's year with the land read from the title (confidence 2). The infobox gives no area.

correction.text: Cliopatria's 936 shape unchanged, valid 936-943 only: the entire Jazira (Mosul, Diyar Rabi'a, Diyar Bakr, Diyar Mudar) under Nasir al-Dawla; Aleppo and northern Syria are added from 944 by the next keyframe

keyframe_review.note: 211,448 km2 for 936-946 (on the gazetteer about 107,000 km2 of Iraq, 57,000 of Turkey and 39,000 of Syria, i.e. Mosul, Diyar Bakr and the Syrian Jazira, plus 3 Iranian border cells): the page has Hasan 'secured control over the entire Jazira by the end of 936'. The shape is right for 936-943; it lacks Aleppo, which Sayf al-Dawla took in October 944 (Sayf al-Dawla page). The dynasty infobox gives no area to compare. [orchestrator 2 Nov 2026: from/to set to 936..943 from this entry's own 'valid 936-943 only'; without them the compiler drew the shape for all its Cliopatria years, overlapping the next keyframe (window p1100-p1199 report)]

correction.text: The Jazira plus northern Syria from Aleppo to Homs, as in Cliopatria's 947 shape without its Iranian, Azerbaijani, Armenian, Georgian and Russian cells: Sayf al-Dawla's Aleppo emirate added to Nasir al-Dawla's Jazira

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Sayf al-Dawla entered Aleppo on 29 October 944 and the October 945 agreement left him 'northern Syria and the Thughur' (Sayf al-Dawla page), so Cliopatria's 947 start is three years late. Damascus (July-December 946) is a passing gain and is in the ledger only.

correction.text: Cliopatria's 947 shape without its Iranian, Azerbaijani, Armenian, Georgian and Russian cells: the Jazira and northern Syria of the pages

keyframe_review.note: 482,214 km2 for 947-959. The shape runs from the Mediterranean (34.7 E, Cilicia) to 49.3 E and 42.0 N. Its Iranian, Azerbaijani, Armenian, Georgian and Russian cells (about 120,000 km2 on the gazetteer: East and West Azerbaijan, Nakhchivan, Karabakh, a few cells at Derbent) are not supported: the Sayf al-Dawla page lists only 'Jund Hims, Jund Qinnasrin, and Jund al-Awasim', 'Most of Diyar Bakr and Diyar Mudar' and nominal suzerainty over the Cilician frontier towns, and the Nasir al-Dawla page records his attempts on Adharbayjan 'in 934 and 938' as failures. The Syrian, Turkish and Iraqi cells fit the pages. The dynasty infobox gives no area to compare.

correction.text: Cliopatria's 960 shape without its Iranian, Azerbaijani, Armenian, Georgian and Russian cells: the Jazira and northern Syria of the pages

keyframe_review.note: 471,822 km2 for 960-961. Same shape as 947-959. Byzantine pressure: Andrassos 960 and Anazarbus in winter 961-962 (Sayf al-Dawla page). The dynasty infobox gives no area to compare.

correction.text: Cliopatria's 962 shape without its Iranian, Azerbaijani, Armenian, Georgian and Russian cells: the Jazira and northern Syria of the pages

keyframe_review.note: 458,350 km2 for 962-969. Cliopatria drops Cilicia (Adana) here, matching 'Winter 961–962: Byzantines captured Anazarbus'; it keeps Antioch and the Syrian coast (Hatay, Latakia cells) until 969, matching 'Michael Bourtzes and Peter took Antioch' in October 969 (Sa'd al-Dawla of Aleppo page). Aleppo was sacked in December 962 but not taken. Same Iranian/Caucasian cells to remove. The dynasty infobox gives no area to compare.

correction.text: Cliopatria's 970 shape without its Iranian, Azerbaijani, Armenian, Georgian and Russian cells: the Jazira and northern Syria of the pages (valid 970-978)

keyframe_review.note: 399,114 km2 for 970-979. Hatay and Latakia are gone, matching the October 969 loss of Antioch; Aleppo is a Byzantine tributary protectorate from December 969 or January 970 and acknowledges Buyid suzerainty in 979 (Sa'd page). The Iraqi Jazira half (Mosul, Ninawa 148 of 148 cells) is right only until the Buyid conquest: 'Adud al-Dawla took Mosul in June 978' and 'the Buyid dissolution of the Hamdanid emirate in 979' (Abu Taghlib page). Valid 970-978 with the Mosul half; 979 is covered by the next keyframe. Same Iranian/Caucasian cells to remove. The dynasty infobox gives no area to compare.

correction.text: The Aleppo emirate of Sa'd al-Dawla after the loss of the Jazira: northern Syria and Diyar Mudar without Raqqa; valid 979-989

keyframe_review.note: 215,128 km2 for 980-989 (Aleppo 58 of 67 cells, Hamah 34 of 37, Homs 111 of 179, Raqqa 68 of 69, Sanliurfa 20 of 73 on the gazetteer, plus about 118,000 km2 of Iranian and Caucasian cells). Right in dropping Mosul (Buyid from 979) and in keeping the Aleppo emirate; wrong in the Iranian/Caucasian cells and in Raqqa, which the page leaves out: 'After acknowledging Buyid suzerainty, Sa'd received Diyar Mudar, except Raqqa and Rahba' (979) and Abu Taghlib had taken Raqqa before 971. Homs: 'Byzantines sacked Homs, which was then returned to Hamdanid control' (October 983); the Sa'id al-Dawla page has Basil's forces taking Homs, Apamea and Shayzar before the treaty of 1000 (year not given), so Homs is uncertain from then.

correction.text: The Aleppo emirate alone, valid 990-1004 (Cliopatria's 980 shape without its Iranian/Caucasian cells and Raqqa); the shape ends with the state in 1004 and is not used for 1005-1027

keyframe_review.note: 399,572 km2 for 990-1027: it adds back Mosul and the Iraqi Jazira (about 107,000 km2 of Iraq on the gazetteer) and the Iranian/Caucasian cells. The Mosul branch ended in 989-990 ('Abu Tahir Ibrahim ibn Nasir al-Dawla (989–990)'; 'After this, their area of control in northern Iraq was divided between the Uqaylids and the Marwanids') and only the Aleppo emirate of Sa'id al-Dawla (991-1002) and Lu'lu' survives to the infobox end of 1004. The shape is also used by Cliopatria for 1004-1027, after the dynasty.

keyframe_review.note: 723,078 km2 for 1028-1033, Iraq, Syria, Saudi Arabia. region.text: Mosul and Diyar Bakr, the governorship of Hasan Nasir al-Dawla

ledger.note: 929: Hasan Nasir al-Dawla governs Mosul and Diyar Bakr, the core of the Hamdanid emirate. 'The rule of Hassan Nasir al-Dawla (929–968), governor of Mosul and Diyar Bakr'; the infobox lists Nasir al-Dawla 929-967 after Abdallah ibn Hamdan (906-929). The infobox's 'Established: 890' (Hamdan ibn Hamdun, Mardin 892-895, Mosul capital from 905) is not used as the start: the Hamdanids are the caliph's governors until 944/947, which is how the Abbasid dossier draws them (vassal_start 929). The Nasir al-Dawla page has his troops occupy Mosul in 934 after Sa'id's murder.

region.text: the entire Jazira: Diyar Rabi'a, Diyar Bakr and Diyar Mudar with Mosul

ledger.note: 936: Nasir al-Dawla holds the whole Jazira. 'in late 935 the caliph al-Radi was forced to formally recognize him as governor of Mosul and of the entire Jazira'; he 'secured control over the entire Jazira by the end of 936' and the revolts in Diyar Bakr and Diyar Mudar were put down by then. This is the 936 Cliopatria shape.

region.text: Baghdad, where the Hamdanids entered as amirs al-umara

ledger.note: 942: Nasir al-Dawla rules the caliph's Baghdad as amir al-umara. 'he had Ibn Ra'iq assassinated and succeeded him as amir al-umara' in early 942 (infobox 18 February 942 to 11 May 943); the page also says 'they entered on 4 June 942'. An occupation of the caliph's capital without annexation: the Jazira stays the state.

region.text: Baghdad

ledger.note: 943: the Hamdanids leave Baghdad. 'when in late 943 a mutiny broke out among their troops' they returned to Mosul and agreed to pay the Turkish amir Tuzun 'an annual tribute of 3.6 million dirhams' in exchange for keeping the Jazira.

region.text: Aleppo and its province

ledger.note: 944: Sayf al-Dawla takes Aleppo. 'Aleppo surrendered without a fight in February 944'; he 'entered the city on 29 October 944' (the dynasty infobox: 'Sayf al-Dawla establishes himself in Aleppo after successfully countering the Ikhshidids of Egypt: 944').

region.text: northern Syria from Aleppo to Homs

ledger.note: 944: the Hamdanids and the Ikhshidids fight for northern Syria. Sayf al-Dawla was 'besieging Homs when he defeated the Ikhshidid army under Kafur, and Homs then opened its gates' (undated); Damascus was occupied briefly in early 945; al-Ikhshid invaded in April-June 945 and Sayf lost a battle and retreated to Raqqa.
944: Aleppo becomes Sayf al-Dawla's main residence beside Mosul (the dynasty infobox: Aleppo 944-1002); the page names 'Aleppo (main residence) and Mayyafariqin (Jaziran provinces)' as his capitals.

region.text: northern Syria down to Homs, recognised by al-Ikhshid

ledger.note: 945: al-Ikhshid recognises the Hamdanids in northern Syria. 'Al-Ikhshid recognized Hamdanid control of northern Syria and the Thughur'; Sayf al-Dawla 'paid an annual tribute to Egypt and gave up his claims on Damascus'. The page names no formal treaty.

region.text: northern Syria from Aleppo to Homs

ledger.note: 945: the October agreement ends the first war for northern Syria; the caliph gave it formal sanction and Sayf married a niece of al-Ikhshid.

region.text: Damascus

ledger.note: 946: Sayf al-Dawla takes Damascus after al-Ikhshid's death. 'July 946: After al-Ikhshid died, Sayf al-Dawla took Damascus.' Kafur defeated him near Ramla in December 946.

region.text: Damascus

ledger.note: 946: the war for Damascus resumes with al-Ikhshid's death in July 946.

region.text: Damascus

ledger.note: 947: Damascus stays Ikhshidid. 'Spring 947: Sayf al-Dawla failed to retake Damascus.' The page does not date the loss itself between the December 946 defeat near Ramla and this attempt.

region.text: Damascus

ledger.note: 947: the fight for Damascus ends. 'The Ikhshidids occupied Aleppo in July 947, then negotiated'; 'The 945 terms were reaffirmed, but the Ikhshidids no longer paid tribute for Damascus' (the reaffirmation is not dated precisely).

region.text: Mosul and Nasibin

ledger.note: 958: the Buyids take Mosul and Nisibis from Nasir al-Dawla. 'Another round of warfare erupted in 956–958. Nasir al-Dawla briefly captured Baghdad, then withdrew', and 'The Buyids captured Mosul and Nasibin' (the page dates the round of warfare 956–958, not the capture itself, so the year is inferred: confidence 2, set by reviewer me-08-d). Terms followed; 'In 964, Nasir al-Dawla tried to renegotiate the terms', but Mu'izz al-Dawla invaded again and captured Mosul and Nasibin, and Nasir was deposed by his son Abu Taghlib in May 967 (Abu Taghlib page). The contest is drawn from 958 to the 974 settlement; the page does not date the withdrawals in between.

region.text: Anazarbus and the Cilician frontier towns under Hamdanid suzerainty

ledger.note: 962: the Byzantines take Anazarbus and Cilicia. 'Winter 961–962: Byzantines captured Anazarbus' and, in mid-December 962, stormed Aleppo except the citadel ('about 10,000 captives'); the page gives Sayf only 'Nominal suzerainty over Byzantine-frontier towns in Cilicia', and 'Tarsus surrendered on 16 August' 965 when 'Cilicia became a Byzantine province'.

region.text: Antioch and the north Syrian littoral

ledger.note: 969: the Byzantines take Antioch. 'Michael Bourtzes and Peter took Antioch, securing their control over the north Syrian littoral' (October 969); in December 969 or January 970 they 'forced Qarquya to sign a treaty making Aleppo a tributary Byzantine protectorate' (Treaty of Safar on the Sayf al-Dawla page): the Byzantine dossier records the vassal tint.

region.text: Mosul and Nasibin

ledger.note: 974: the Buyids settle with Abu Taghlib. 'In 973, Hamdan finally persuaded Bakhtiyar to march north'; the conflict 'ended in a settlement in 974' that gave Abu Taghlib the laqab Uddat al-Dawla and required tribute. He held all of Diyar Bakr and Diyar Mudar by 971.

region.text: Mosul and the Jazira

ledger.note: 978: Adud al-Dawla takes Mosul. 'Bakhtiyar and Abu Taghlib were defeated in a battle near Samarra' in May 978 and 'Adud al-Dawla took Mosul in June 978'; Abu Taghlib fled through Nisibis and Mayyafariqin to Rahba and then Fatimid southern Syria.

region.text: the Jazira with Mosul

ledger.note: 979: the Jazira passes to the Buyids. 'after the Buyid dissolution of the Hamdanid emirate in 979' (Abu Taghlib page); the Buyid dynasty page lists 'the Jazira (979)' among Adud al-Dawla's additions.

region.text: Diyar Mudar except Raqqa and Rahba (Harran and Edessa/Urfa)

ledger.note: 979: the Aleppo branch receives Diyar Mudar. 'After acknowledging Buyid suzerainty, Sa'd received Diyar Mudar, except Raqqa and Rahba'; the caliph gave him the laqab Sa'd al-Dawla.

region.text: Mosul and the Jazira

ledger.note: 979: Abu Taghlib dies and the fight for the Jazira ends. 'He was captured and executed after the battle of 29 August 979 at Ramla, likely at Adud al-Dawla's behest.'

region.text: Mosul, held by two Hamdanid sons of Nasir al-Dawla as Buyid governors

ledger.note: 989: Hamdanid governors return to Mosul under the Buyids. 'The Jazira remained under Buyid control until 989'; Abu Taghlib's brothers Husayn and Ibrahim, 'who had served the Buyids, were installed as governors to oppose the Kurdish chieftain Badh ibn Dustak'; the dynasty page lists them as rulers 989-990.

region.text: Mosul and Diyar Rabi'a

ledger.note: 990: the Uqaylids end Hamdanid rule at Mosul. 'After this, their area of control in northern Iraq was divided between the Uqaylids and the Marwanids' (infobox: Mosul 905-990). The Uqaylid page has Mosul and Diyar Rabi'a occupied 'in 989' and the Banu Uqayl turning on the Hamdanids (Abu Taghlib page), so the year is 989 or 990.

region.text: the share of the former Hamdanid area that went to the Marwanids

ledger.note: 990: the Marwanids take their share. The page says only that the area 'was divided between the Uqaylids and the Marwanids'; the region is inferred from the Marwanid seat (the Marwanid dossier dates the retaking of Hisn Kayfa to 991). A gap-filler should read the Marwanid page.
990: Aleppo is the Hamdanid capital alone. Infobox 'Mosul (905–990)', 'Aleppo (944–1002)'.

1002: Lu'lu' takes direct power at Aleppo. 'in January 1002 Sa'id al-Dawla died, possibly poisoned by Lu'lu''; 'Lu'lu' now assumed direct power, at first as ostensible guardians over Sa'id al-Dawla's sons' (Lu'lu' al-Kabir page: 'Along with his son Mansur, Lu'lu' now assumed direct power over Aleppo'). Hamdanid princes remain nominal until exiled to Egypt.

region.text: the Aleppo emirate of the last Hamdanids

ledger.note: 1004: the last Hamdanid rule ends at Aleppo. Infobox 'Disestablished: 1004'; the text says 'in 1003 the Fatimids deposed the Hamdanids'; Lu'lu' 'had them exiled to Egypt' in 1003/4 (Sa'id al-Dawla page), and Mansur ibn Lu'lu' was deposed in 1015/16, 'ending the last vestiges of Hamdanid rule in Aleppo'. Lu'lu' ruled Aleppo as a Fatimid-recognising regime (995, 'acknowledged him as Caliph'); the Emirate of Aleppo page has the city 'eventually falling to the Fatimids in 1017'.

wars.name: Hamdanid-Ikhshidid war for Syria

zones.text: northern Syria from Aleppo to Homs

wars.outcome: Sayf al-Dawla took Aleppo (29 October 944), lost Damascus twice and kept northern Syria and the Thughur by the October 945 agreement, with an annual tribute to Egypt; war resumed after al-Ikhshid's death in July 946 and ended in 947 with the 945 terms reaffirmed and no tribute for Damascus.
wars.note: Dates from the Sayf al-Dawla page: Damascus early 945; al-Ikhshid's invasion April-June 945; Damascus July 946; Ramla December 946; spring 947; Aleppo occupied July 947.

wars.name: Byzantine-Hamdanid wars of Sayf al-Dawla
wars.outcome: Raids and counter-raids on the Cilician and Syrian frontier (Charpete 938, Hadath 948/954/957, Marash 953, Andrassos 960, Raban, Anazarbus 961-962), the sack of Aleppo in December 962, the Byzantine province of Cilicia in 965 and the fall of Antioch in October 969.
wars.note: The page dates Raban only as 'Spring after 957'; the Nasir al-Dawla page and others may differ.

wars.name: Buyid-Hamdanid wars over Mosul
wars.outcome: Mu'izz al-Dawla defeated Nasir al-Dawla in January 946, the war was renewed in 948 (tribute and the Buyid names in the Friday prayer), 956-958 (Baghdad briefly taken, Mosul and Nisibis lost in 958) and 964 (Mosul and Nisibis taken again); under Abu Taghlib Bakhtiyar marched north in 973 and settled in 974; Adud al-Dawla took Mosul in June 978 and dissolved the emirate in 979.
wars.note: Years from the Nasir al-Dawla page (946, 948, 956-958, 964) and the Abu Taghlib page (973-974, 978-979).

wars.name: Hamdanid campaign against the Fatimids in Syria
wars.outcome: Abu Taghlib, driven from the Jazira, failed to win Damascus from the rebel al-Qassam and was defeated and executed after the battle of Ramla on 29 August 979.

wars.name: Byzantine conquest of Antioch and the Treaty of Safar

zones.text: Antioch and the north Syrian littoral

wars.outcome: Antioch and the littoral fell in October 969; a treaty of December 969 or January 970 made Aleppo a tributary Byzantine protectorate under Qarquya, with Bakjur as his successor.

wars.name: Bakjur's revolt and the Fatimid attacks on Aleppo
wars.outcome: Bakjur deposed Qarquya in 975; Sa'd retook Aleppo in 977 and Bakjur got Homs; Bakjur attacked Aleppo with Fatimid support in September 983 and Basil II's general Bardas Phokas relieved it; Bakjur was captured and executed after Na'ura in April 991; the Fatimid al-Aziz attacked in 992 and Manjutakin again in spring 994 and retreated to Damascus; in 995 the emperor released the emirate from tribute.
wars.note: Sa'id al-Dawla page for 992-995; Sa'd page for 975-991.

wars.name: Byzantine-Hamdanid war of 995-1001 (Basil II)
wars.outcome: Basil's forces took Homs, Apamea and Shayzar and besieged Aleppo for eleven months; a peace treaty of 1000 guaranteed Aleppo's survival as a buffer state and a ten-year truce followed in 1001.
wars.note: The extract does not date the capture of Homs, Apamea and Shayzar; the treaty is 1000 in the introduction and 1001 in the body.

wars.name: Uqaylid conquest of Mosul
wars.outcome: The Banu Uqayl occupied Mosul and Diyar Rabi'a in 989 against the Buyids and then turned on the Hamdanid governors, killing Abu Tahir Ibrahim; Uqaylid rule is founded in 990.
wars.note: The Uqaylid page gives 989 for the occupation and 990 for the founding; the Hamdanid page gives 989-990 for the last Mosul rulers.

certainty.note: No treaty line or survey fixes any Hamdanid frontier; the Jazira, the Byzantine marches and the Syrian desert edge are approximate. The October 945 agreement with the Ikhshidids and the 969/970 and 1000 Byzantine treaties name zones, not lines.

notes: Row question (data/README, brief section 6). Cliopatria's 'Hamdanid Emirates' (936-1259, 23 shapes) is four things: (1) 936-1003, the real Hamdanids, the Jazira of Mosul and the Aleppo emirate; (2) 1004-1027, the same 990 shape carried on after the dynasty; (3) 1028-1259, fifteen shapes (centroid 60 E 30 N for 1210-1249, Derbent for 1126-1191, Arabia for 1250-1259) that are not Hamdanid at all and are marked wrong with an empty correction; no page opened says which state or states they really draw, so the Cliopatria data fixer should relabel the row; the 1028-1055 shape (723,000 km2, Iraq, Syria and 129,000 km2 of Saudi Arabia) is the one most likely to be a real state of its own. Start: this dossier starts in 929 (Nasir al-Dawla, 'governor of Mosul and Diyar Bakr') because the Abbasid dossier opens a vassal span for the Hamdanids in 929 and 947; the infobox's 'Established: 890' (Hamdan ibn Hamdun, Mardin 892-895) and Mosul as capital from 905 (Abdallah ibn Hamdan 906-929) are not drawn. End: 1004 (infobox); the Sa'id al-Dawla page puts 'the last vestiges of Hamdanid rule in Aleppo' in 1015/6 and the Emirate of Aleppo page puts the Fatimid take-over in 1017. Two branches: Mosul (Nasir al-Dawla 929-967, Abu Taghlib 967-978, a last Buyid-appointed pair 989-990) and Aleppo (Sayf al-Dawla 945-967, Sa'd al-Dawla 967-991, Sa'id al-Dawla 991-1002); the dossier treats them as one state because Cliopatria and Wikipedia do. No single ruler strip is possible (the reigns overlap), so rulers are omitted. Sa'd's Aleppo was a Byzantine tributary from December 969/January 970 (the Byzantine dossier has the vassal_start/end 970-1004), acknowledged Buyid suzerainty in 979 and Fatimid suzerainty in December 986; those relations are the overlords' events and are not repeated here. Unsettled within the 9-page budget: (a) the Cliopatria 947-979 shapes carry about 120,000 km2 of Iranian and Caucasian cells (West and East Azerbaijan, Nakhchivan, Karabakh, Derbent) that no page supports: corrected away; (b) Homs, Apamea and Shayzar (the Sa'id page has Basil's forces take them before the treaty of 1000, no year) and Hama, Kinnasrin and Latakia after 969 are not in any page's extract, so the Aleppo shape after 983 keeps Homs and Hamah at confidence 2; (c) Raqqa and Rahba: Abu Taghlib held Raqqa before 971 and Sa'd's 979 grant excludes both, but who held Raqqa 979-1004 is not stated; (d) the Marwanid share of 990 (confidence 1); (e) the Mosul takeover is 989 on the Uqaylid page and 990 on the dynasty page; (f) Nasir al-Dawla page puts Mosul in his hands in 934, the dynasty page in 929; (g) no page gives an infobox area, so no area comparison was possible; (h) the Emirate of Aleppo page and the Sa'd al-Dawla disambiguation page were thin. Gazetteer: all names used exist (Ar Raqqah, Homs (Hims), Lattakia, Hatay, Sanliurfa, Diyarbakir, Ninawa, Adana, Antakya, Nusaybin, Jazira, Aleppo (region)); Diyar Bakr, Diyar Mudar, Diyar Rabi'a and the Thughur are not regions in the gazetteer and are approximated by provinces. Counterparts: ikhshidid-dynasty, uqaylid-dynasty, marwanids-of-diyar-bakr, byzantine-empire, buyid-dynasty, fatimid-caliphate, mirdasid-dynasty exist; a dossier for Bakjur's Homs/Damascus governorship (977-988) is not needed.
